nodes.name: Eternal Empire
nodes.summary: Oriathan/imperial civilisation, also called the Sarn Empire, founded in 1 IC by Azmeri migrants under Tarcus Veruso on the ruins of the Vaal capital. Ruled by Emperors from Sarn, it held most of central Wraeclast with a Roman-style legion system until the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) destroyed it; Oriath survived as its successor.

chronology.relative: 1 IC to c. 1339 IC; roughly 260 years before PoE1 (1599-1600 IC)

sources.locator: lead paragraph and sections 'History' through 'The Cataclysm'
Act 1: Cemetery of the Eternals / Eternal prison areas

nodes.name: Azmeri
nodes.summary: Ancient tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who worship Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi and others. Eighty thousand of them under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Eternal Empire in 1 IC; the Azmeri of the Forest Encampment and the Wildwood descend from those who stayed behind.

nodes.name: Order of the Templar
nodes.summary: Theocratic order led by a High Templar that worships Innocence. Within the Eternal Empire it produced figures such as High Templars Andronicus and Voll; after the Cataclysm it governed the unaffected island of Oriath as the Templar Theocracy, with Dominus and Avarius as its PoE1-era High Templars.

nodes.name: Gemling Legion
nodes.summary: Elite legions of the Eternal Empire created by Malachai: legionnaires infused with virtue gems, led by Captains, which gave the Empire military dominance. Chitus carried a master gem whose heartbeat bound every gemling to his own, so they fell when he died; survivors were transformed by the Cataclysm into the Undying.

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: Coalition led by High Templar Voll of Thebrus against Chitus' gem-and-thaumaturgy 'thaumatocracy'. Its supporters included Victario, Ondar, Geofri, Kastov and Adus, with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies.

nodes.name: Perandus family
nodes.summary: Wealthiest merchant-lender family of the Eternal Empire (motto 'With piety and justice'). Blocked from the throne by the Phrecians, they rigged Izaro's Labyrinth so Chitus Perandus won; Cadiro looted the treasury before the fall. Descendants include Syndicate member Janus Perandus.

sources.locator: forum announcement describing Cadiro's stolen treasury and indebted dead

nodes.name: Phrecian dynasty
nodes.summary: Unbroken line of emperors descended from Alano Phrecia, who founded the line after killing the 'dark being' in 35 IC. It ran from Alano through Romira and Tyndarus to Izaro, who was childless.

sources.locator: sections 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' to 'Reign of Izaro'

nodes.name: The Godless Three
nodes.summary: Three thaumaturgists trained by Malachai: Shavronne of Umbra, Maligaro the Inquisitor and Doedre Darktongue. Maligaro and Doedre were burned by Voll; Malachai later revived all three to guard his heart, lungs and entrails.

nodes.name: Maraketh
nodes.summary: Desert people of the Vastiri led by Sekhemas, living in akhara (tribes). In 1333 IC Sekhema Deshret joined the Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains; later, Deshret sealed the Highgate mines. A large tribe lives at Highgate in PoE1; the Ardura akhara and Sekhema Asala appear in PoE2.

nodes.name: Faridun
nodes.summary: Maraketh rejects (flawed or mutated newborns left in the dunes) raised by wandering Faridun tribes in the Vastiri, who accept necromancy and long for reunification with the akharas. In PoE2 Act 2 the Countess recruits them with the promise of resurrecting Jamanra.

nodes.name: Karui
nodes.summary: Seafaring warrior people of the southern archipelago. Under King Kaom they allied with Voll's Purity Rebellion, took Lioneye's Watch and founded the first Karui settlement on the mainland; Kaom later fell at Highgate. The Empire had enslaved Karui under Chitus.

nodes.name: Ezomytes
nodes.summary: Clan people of Ezomyr, subjugated and enslaved by the Eternal Empire. Thane Rigwald rallied them in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion of 1333 IC and they joined the siege of Sarn.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamity and guard dangerous artefacts. Icius Perandus and, much later, Janus Perandus belonged to it.

nodes.name: The Undying
nodes.summary: Gemlings and citizens of Sarn transformed by the Cataclysm into mindless monsters that can live for centuries; some gemling legionnaires later regain sentience (Act 8 Grain Gate).

nodes.name: Sarn
nodes.summary: Capital of the Eternal Empire, founded by Veruso on the site of Azala Vaal. Burned during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons, rebuilt, besieged by Voll in 1334 IC and fallen within an hour of the Cataclysm. The Act 8 city of the exile.

nodes.name: Azala Vaal
nodes.summary: Former capital of the Vaal Empire; Tarcus Veruso planted his banner here to found Sarn and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Highgate
nodes.summary: Mountain region where Veruso buried the virtue gems ('Tears of Maji'), where slaves mined them under Chitus, where Malachai placed the Rapture Device and the Beast lies beneath, and where a Maraketh tribe lives in PoE1.

sources.locator: 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Slave trade', 'Reign of Voll'

nodes.name: Oriath
nodes.summary: Island off the south-east of Wraeclast, founded by Innocence's banished followers and ruled by the Templar theocracy from Theopolis. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it served as the Empire's successor; destroyed in the Atlas storyline of PoE1 and revisited in PoE2 Act 4.

nodes.name: Theopolis
nodes.summary: Capital of Oriath and seat of the High Templar; home of the Grand Arena where Daresso fought.

nodes.name: Lioneye's Watch
nodes.summary: Southern Eternal garrison commanded by General Marceus Lioneye, taken by Kaom's Karui in the Purity Rebellion; later the survivors' town in PoE1 Acts 1 and 6.

nodes.name: Axiom Prison
nodes.summary: Eternal outpost warded by Brutus where Shavronne of Umbra experimented on him; blocked Karui advance.

nodes.name: Chamber of Sins
nodes.summary: Laboratory built by Chitus where Maligaro conducted flesh experiments, opposed by nearby Phrecia Cathedral; named by Archbishop Geofri.

nodes.name: Phrecia Cathedral
nodes.summary: Cathedral seat of Archbishop Geofri in the Phrecian heartlands (today the Fellshrine Ruins); Geofri was killed here by Maligaro.

nodes.name: The Grain Gate
nodes.summary: Sarn gate attacked by the Purity forces; failed assault repelled by Chitus' gemlings. Gemlings survive there in Act 8.

nodes.name: The Crystal Veins
nodes.summary: Highgate caverns holding the Rapture Device, which the exile reactivates to enter the Beast.

nodes.name: The Dried Lake
nodes.summary: Place where Voll fled after the Cataclysm and wrote his Confession; he and his undead legion remained there for centuries.

nodes.name: The Lord's Labyrinth
nodes.summary: Trap-filled maze built by Emperor Izaro in Sarn to pick his successor, opened 1317 IC. Chitus won it; the exile later challenges it to earn ascendancy points.

nodes.name: Cemetery of the Eternals
nodes.summary: PoE2 Act 1 area in Ogham where Eternal praetors are entombed, with inscriptions claiming the land 'in life and death'.

nodes.name: Trarthus
nodes.summary: Land south-west of Wraeclast used by the Empire as an exile colony; rebelled in 870 IC.

nodes.name: Chamber of Innocence
nodes.summary: Templar chamber in Oriath built under High Templar Avarius whose stained glass windows tell the Sin and Innocence story.

nodes.name: Virtue Gems
nodes.summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.

nodes.name: Thaumaturgy
nodes.summary: Gem-based magic whose source is the Beast. Outlawed by Veruso, embraced by Chitus under Malachai's 'Thaumatocracy', and banned again by Voll.

nodes.name: Ascendancy
nodes.summary: Power granted to the exile who completes Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth trials; framed as inheriting the Labyrinth's succession test.

nodes.name: Eternal calendar
nodes.summary: Calendar of 1 IC (Imperialis Conceptus), seven days and thirteen moons (Verusi, Divini, Derivi ... Azmeri).

nodes.name: Lord's Trial
nodes.summary: Azmerian maze-festival to choose chieftains; raised Veruso to power and inspired Izaro's Labyrinth.

nodes.name: Eternal slave trade
nodes.summary: Under Chitus the Empire enslaved Karui, Ezomytes and Maraketh, sending them to mines and cities.

nodes.name: Ankh of Eternity
nodes.summary: Resurrection artefact used by Veruso to revive Chiara; per Clarissa the ritual produced a monster. Later hidden in the Quay.

nodes.name: Rapture Device
nodes.summary: Device Malachai built in the Solaris Temple, claimed able to kill the Beast. Powered by the Eyes of Fury and Desire and Dialla's life force, it tore into the Beast so Malachai could enter.

nodes.name: Transmutia Device
nodes.summary: Device given by Malachai to Maligaro to manipulate virtue gems; later the exile's crafting bench.

nodes.name: Black Elixir
nodes.summary: Poison from the Baleful Gem and Black Death venom, used by Ondar to kill Chitus.

nodes.name: Chitus' master gem
nodes.summary: Large gem in Chitus' chest linking each gemling's heartbeat to his.

sources.locator: Issue 4 The Black Heart, p. 11 (cited by wiki)

nodes.name: Deshret's Banner
nodes.summary: Key to opening the seal on the Highgate mines; taken by Voll after killing Deshret, retrieved in Act 4.

nodes.name: Wings of Vastiri
nodes.summary: Maraketh symbol of office taken by Titucius, retrieved from his undead remains in Act 4.

nodes.name: Eye of Fury
nodes.summary: Taken from Kaom at Highgate, used to power the Rapture Device.

nodes.name: Eye of Desire
nodes.summary: Taken from Daresso's spirit, used to power the Rapture Device.

nodes.name: Star of Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Necklace with a virtue gem from Kalisa Maas that turned Merveil into a siren.

nodes.name: Golden Pages
nodes.summary: Vaal artefacts describing the Vaal Cataclysm that Malachai had Icius Perandus translate (wiki: 'possibly the Golden Pages'); the translation inspired the Reverie Device.

nodes.name: Reverie Device
nodes.summary: Malachai's map-using precursor of the Map Device used to enter the Nightmare.

nodes.name: Sign of Purity
nodes.summary: Weapon forged from Innocence's blood, gifted to the first High Templar; used by the exile in Act 5-10.

sources.locator: Act 5 dialogue: The Sign of Purity

nodes.name: Dark Ember
nodes.summary: Seed Sin planted beneath Highgate; the Beast grew from it.

nodes.name: Letters from Chitus
nodes.summary: Three letters from Chitus to Cadiro (1316-1318 IC) planning to win Izaro's Labyrinth. Released as physical GGG merchandise.

nodes.name: The Purity Chronicles
nodes.summary: Six-book chronicle by Garivaldi in the Library of Sarn (Act 3 area) on the Purity Rebellion.

nodes.name: Voll's Confession
nodes.summary: Voll's confession that he trusted the most corrupt of men.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Origins
nodes.summary: Official comic recounting Victario, the Karui Way, the Chamber of Sins and Chitus' death.

nodes.name: Chamber of Innocence stained glass windows
nodes.summary: Templar propaganda in Oriath depicting Innocence as pure and Sin as deceitful twin; later contradicted by Lycia.

nodes.name: Lycia's relics
nodes.summary: Forbidden Sanctum relics revealing the Original Sin and Innocence's ascension.

nodes.name: Tarcus Veruso
nodes.summary: Azmeri leader and first Emperor (Prima Imperialus) who led 80,000 Azmeri to found Sarn in 1 IC. A ruthless despot, he outlawed thaumaturgy, buried the gems under Highgate, and created the legion system.

nodes.name: Chiara
nodes.summary: Wife of Veruso; died in childbirth; Ankh ritual reportedly made her a monster.

nodes.name: Egrin
nodes.summary: Young Azmeri whose visions may have led the descent; later cast out and taken in by the Order of the Djinn.

nodes.name: Caspiro
nodes.summary: Second Emperor, a low-born legionnaire who survived a labyrinth trial; dismembered by a dark being five years after Veruso's death.

nodes.name: Alano Phrecia
nodes.summary: General who defeated the dark being in 35 IC, sealed it away and was crowned Emperor, founding the Phrecian line.

nodes.name: Romira Phrecian
nodes.summary: Emperor who fed his wife's sons (fathered by his brother) back to her; deposed in the Night of a Thousand Ribbons.

nodes.name: Tyndarus Phrecius
nodes.summary: Emperor c. 870-892 IC, backed by High Templar Andronicus; lost the Trarthan war of independence.

nodes.name: Izaro Phrecius
nodes.summary: Last Phrecian Emperor; childless, he built the Lord's Labyrinth to choose a successor. Chitus won it, then sealed Izaro inside. The exile fights him in the Labyrinth.

nodes.name: Chitus Perandus
nodes.summary: Perandus who rigged the Lord's Labyrinth, poisoned the Ezomyte slave Weylin, and became Emperor in 1319 IC. Brutal, vain, ruled with Malachai's gemling thaumatocracy; killed by Ondar at the Night of a Thousand Ribbons in 1334 IC.

nodes.name: Julius Perandus
nodes.summary: Father of Chitus.

nodes.name: Cadiro Perandus
nodes.summary: Chitus' uncle, patron of Prospero; engineered Perandus' win, surrendered Sarn to Voll, and hid the treasury, binding debtors in undeath to guard it.

nodes.name: Icius Perandus
nodes.summary: Scholar to the Empire, translated Vaal artefacts for Malachai, hid the Golden Pages, joined the Order of the Djinn.

nodes.name: Malachai
nodes.summary: Laureate Thaumaturge to Chitus, creator of the gemling legions and Rapture Device. Spared by Voll, he entered the Beast and caused the Cataclysm. Defeated by the exile in Act 4.

nodes.name: Lazhwar
nodes.summary: Archbishop of the Eternal Faith whose thaumaturgy and Eternal Laboratory work preceded Malachai's.

nodes.name: Lady Dialla
nodes.summary: Malachai's concubine and promised Gemling Queen; jewels set along her spine. Refused to sacrifice herself in the Rapture Device and survived centuries. Met in Act 3.

nodes.name: Maligaro
nodes.summary: Inquisitor Maligaro, flesh artist of the Godless Three; burned by Voll, his spirit lived on in Maligaro's Sanctum; killed in Act 7.

nodes.name: Doedre
nodes.summary: Doedre Darktongue (Stamatis), curse-obsessed pupil of Maligaro/member of the Godless Three; burned by Voll; revived by Malachai; fought in Act 4 (Harvest), Act 8 (Doedre's Cesspool) and Act 9 (Rotting Core).

sources.locator: 'until the player character defeats her in Act 8'; 'In-game encounters'

nodes.name: Shavronne of Umbra
nodes.summary: Vain thaumaturge of the Godless Three who experimented on Brutus at Axiom Prison.

nodes.name: Raulo (Fidelitas)
nodes.summary: Maligaro's slave and lover, injected with Calibric Extantia and renamed Fidelitas.

nodes.name: Brutus
nodes.summary: Warden of Axiom Prison; his transformation by Shavronne drove him mad; Act 1 boss.

nodes.name: Voll of Thebrus
nodes.summary: High Templar who led the Purity Rebellion, crowned Emperor 1334 IC, spared Malachai, and perished in the Cataclysm; undead at Dried Lake and defeated in Act 4.

nodes.name: Victario Nevalius
nodes.summary: Poet who stirred rebellion with graffiti and letters to Rigwald; died in the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Marylene
nodes.summary: Victario's lover, died shielding him at the Grain Gate.

nodes.name: Lord Mayor Ondar
nodes.summary: Sarn's Lord Mayor, betrayed and killed Chitus with a Black Elixir weapon, then was cut down by Chitus.

nodes.name: Archbishop Geofri
nodes.summary: Archbishop of Phrecia Cathedral killed by Maligaro; undead guardian in Act 2.

nodes.name: General Adus
nodes.summary: Commander of Highgate who joined Voll; sheltered in Highgate Refinery; killed in Act 9.

nodes.name: Gaius Sentari
nodes.summary: Ezomyte slavemaster and governor beaten at Glarryn; ran Highgate 'civilization camps'.

nodes.name: Marceus Lioneye
nodes.summary: Gem-eyed archer general at Lioneye's Watch, killed by Kaom.

nodes.name: Hector Titucius
nodes.summary: Ezomyte-born gemling general, 'Scourge of the Maraketh', destroyed by Deshret's storm trap in 1333 IC.

nodes.name: Thane Rigwald
nodes.summary: Ezomyte thane who killed King Skothe and led the Bloody Flowers Rebellion.

nodes.name: Weylin
nodes.summary: Ezomyte slave poisoned by Chitus in the Labyrinth.

nodes.name: King Kaom
nodes.summary: Karui king who took Lioneye's Watch, was lured to Highgate by Malachai's voice posing as Tukohama and slain; defeated in Act 4.

nodes.name: Lavianga
nodes.summary: Karui scholar-advisor to Kaom.

nodes.name: Queen Hyrri Ngamaku
nodes.summary: Kaom's niece, archer, led Karui archers at Lioneye's Watch and the Karui at the Grain Gate; after Kaom's death guided the remaining 500 Karui families home, became queen, had a child with Victario (per wiki) and was succeeded by her daughter Ahuana; later vanished.

sources.locator: Lore: 'She later became the queen and had a child with Victario ... succeeded by her daughter, Ahuana'

nodes.name: Sekhema Deshret
nodes.summary: Red Sekhema who destroyed Titucius' legion, sealed the Highgate mines, and was killed by Voll; spirit rescued in Act 9.

nodes.name: Daresso
nodes.summary: King of Swords of Theopolis' Grand Arena; left Oriath c. 1450 IC to cure Merveil; spirit used by Malachai; defeated in Act 4. Chronology caveat: the wiki dates his departure c. 1450 IC yet says his spirit was already used by Malachai (Eye of Desire, 1336 IC) and had been dead ~100 years; the wiki itself calls this 'inexplicable'.

nodes.name: Merveil
nodes.summary: Daresso's wife transformed into a siren by the Star of Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Dominus
nodes.summary: High Templar in PoE1's era who exiled criminals to Wraeclast; killed by the exile atop the Sceptre of God in Act 3.

nodes.name: High Templar Avarius
nodes.summary: Replaced Dominus in Oriath; vessel of Innocence; built the Templar Courts; killed by exile Act 5.

nodes.name: Lycia
nodes.summary: Former Templar who uncovered the real story of Sin and Innocence.

nodes.name: High Templar Venarius
nodes.summary: Historical High Templar who commissioned Valdo Caeserius to build a map device.

nodes.name: High Templar Andronicus
nodes.summary: High Templar backing Tyndarus Phrecius c. 870 IC.

nodes.name: Janus Perandus
nodes.summary: Chitus' great-grandson; Immortal Syndicate member who betrayed the Order of the Djinn.

nodes.name: Solerai
nodes.summary: Legendary Maraketh Sekhema who with Lundara ended the Winter of the World; possibly Solaris.

nodes.name: Lundara
nodes.summary: Twin sister Sekhema; possibly Lunaris.

nodes.name: Jamanra, the Risen King
nodes.summary: Faridun revolutionary leader resurrected by corruption in PoE2 Act 2, given death by Asala.

nodes.name: Sekhema Asala
nodes.summary: Ardura Sekhema in PoE2 who opens the Halani Gates and kills Jamanra, accepting Faridun warriors.

nodes.name: Praetor Draven
nodes.summary: Eternal praetor entombed in the Cemetery of the Eternals; PoE2 Act 1 Memorial key.

nodes.name: Asinia, the Praetor's Consort
nodes.summary: Draven's consort, boss in Tomb of the Consort in PoE2 Act 1.

nodes.name: Sin
nodes.summary: God, brother (twin, per the stained-glass windows) of Innocence; planted the Dark Ember beneath Highgate from which the Beast grew. In PoE2 he is LIKELY the Hooded One (wiki: 'likely Sin', not explicitly confirmed in the corpus).

sources.locator: 'The Hooded One was likely Sin, owing to his dark appearance, apparent godhood and original planting of the Dark Ember'

nodes.name: Innocence
nodes.summary: Templar god, twin of Sin; ascended using hatred of Sin; Oriath's founding deity; also Maxarius.

nodes.name: Garukhan
nodes.summary: Goddess of wind and sky, formerly the Maraketh Sekhema Orbala ('Sekhema of Sekhemas'); freed Sin from the cliff where Innocence's followers had chained him, became his lover and wife and bore Shakari; Sin planted the Dark Ember 'for Garukhan'.

sources.locator: 'Garukhan, Queen of the Wind' (Orbala; Chains of Castigation, Blood of Innocence, Sin 'Garukhan' dialogue)

nodes.name: Prospero
nodes.summary: Azmerian god of the underworld, patron of Cadiro.

nodes.name: Imperialis Conceptus
nodes.summary: Founding of the Eternal Empire (1 IC).

nodes.name: Alano Phrecia defeats the dark being
nodes.summary: Alano sealed the dark being in 35 IC; darkness lifted.

nodes.name: Night of a Thousand Ribbons
nodes.summary: Burning of Sarn in protest against Romira; later festival where Chitus was assassinated.

nodes.name: Trarthan War of Independence
nodes.summary: 870-872 IC rebellion against Tyndarus.

nodes.name: Opening of the Lord's Labyrinth
nodes.summary: Izaro opens the maze on 1317 IC; Chitus and Weylin enter; Chitus poisons Weylin.

nodes.name: Chitus crowned Emperor
nodes.summary: Crowned 1319 IC; seals Izaro in.

nodes.name: Bloody Flowers Rebellion
nodes.summary: 1333 IC Ezomyte victory at Glarryn.

nodes.name: Battle of Lioneye's Watch
nodes.summary: Kaom's ambush kills Lioneye.

nodes.name: Defeat of Titucius
nodes.summary: 3rd Galvano of Vitali 1333 IC; Maraketh storm trap.

nodes.name: Death of Geofri
nodes.summary: 1332 IC; Maligaro ambushes templars.

nodes.name: Siege of Sarn
nodes.summary: Divini 1334 IC; Voll besieges Sarn.

nodes.name: Assassination of Chitus
nodes.summary: Ondar kills Chitus; gemlings fall.

nodes.name: Voll crowned Emperor
nodes.summary: Voll of Thebrus crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC (Eternal Empire page: a week after Cadiro's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci; Purity Chronicles Book 1 says the 2nd Sacrato of Phreci).

nodes.name: Rapture Device activation
nodes.summary: 1336 IC; Dialla refuses; Malachai enters Beast.

nodes.name: The Cataclysm
nodes.summary: c. 1339 IC; Malachai takes control of the Beast; Empire falls.

nodes.name: Deshret seals the mines
nodes.summary: Twenty years after Kaom.

nodes.name: Kaom at Highgate
nodes.summary: Kaom slays his 500 warriors deceived by the Beast.

nodes.name: Original Sin
nodes.summary: Innocence turns followers against Sin.

nodes.name: Creation of the Beast
nodes.summary: Sin plants Dark Ember.

nodes.name: Founding of Oriath
nodes.summary: Templars banished from the Azmeri found Oriath.

nodes.name: Daresso leaves Oriath
nodes.summary: c. 1450 IC (History of Wraeclast); contradicts the use of his spirit's Eye of Desire in 1336 IC, which the wiki leaves unexplained.

nodes.name: Templars shift to Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Malachai spared by Voll
nodes.summary: Malachai promises end of thaumaturgy.

nodes.name: Sceptre of God
nodes.summary: Imperial palace tower of Sarn where Chitus, Malachai and Dialla held court (concubines kept there); the exile kills Dominus atop it in Act 3.

nodes.name: Solaris Temple
nodes.summary: Sarn temple where Malachai built the Rapture Device over more than a year; the exile meets Dialla on Level 2 in Act 3.

nodes.name: Ngamakanui
nodes.summary: Karui homeland archipelago, seat of Kaom and Hyrri; where Voll sought Kaom's help.

nodes.name: Battle at the Grain Gate
nodes.summary: Rebel assault led by Victario with Templars, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Karui; repulsed by Chitus' gemlings, Marylene died shielding Victario.

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Kaom
nodes.summary: Voll and Victario visit Kaom in Ngamakanui; Voll promises Karui sovereignty over Wraeclast's south shore and freedom for slaves in exchange for attacking Lioneye's Watch.

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Deshret
nodes.summary: Voll promises Sekhema Deshret the return of the Vastiri Plains for Maraketh support; she demands Titucius' skin for a saddle.

nodes.name: Kaom's march on Highgate and death
nodes.summary: Lured by the Beast's voice posing as Tukohama, Kaom led 500 warriors to Highgate and was deceived into slaying them before dying; his Eye of Fury was taken.

sources.locator: 'Lioneye's Watch' subsection, Kaom's march to Highgate

nodes.name: Gemlings fall with Chitus
nodes.summary: With Chitus' death his master gem stopped and the legionnaires linked to his heartbeat died; Captain Alsarus' legion survived beyond the perimeter.

nodes.name: Death of Voll
nodes.summary: Voll fled to the Dried Lake after the Cataclysm, remained undead for centuries, and is killed by the exile in Act 4 (quest Breaking the Seal).

nodes.name: Surrender of Sarn
nodes.summary: Cadiro Perandus negotiates Sarn's unconditional surrender to Voll on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC after stealing the treasury.

edges.description: Veruso led 80,000 Azmeri down from the Azmerian ranges and planted his banner on Azala Vaal, founding Sarn and the Empire in 1 IC.
Veruso led eighty thousand Azmeri tribesmen out of the ranges.

sources.locator: 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)': "Eighty thousand tribesmen and women"

edges.description: Veruso founded Sarn as the capital of the Empire.
Sarn was founded on the ruins of the Vaal capital Azala Vaal.
The Empire was founded by Azmeri migrants.
1 IC marks the start of the Eternal calendar and of the Empire.
Veruso led the descent and founded Sarn.
The founding took place at Azala Vaal.
The Azmeri descended into lands left behind by the Vaal Empire after the Vaal Cataclysm.
The wiki says the Empire was 'largely survived by the island of Oriath' and that the Templars shifted their base there after the Cataclysm; 'successor' is an interpretation.
The Empire rose on Vaal ruins and inherited Vaal virtue gems; Veruso forbade a repeat of Vaal folly.
Egrin, cast out for visions, was taken in by the Order of the Djinn.
Egrin's visions may have led the Azmeri descent (speculative).

sources.locator: 'The Azmeri': "may have been led by the visions of a young Azmeri, Egrin"

edges.description: Veruso used the Ankh with an Azmerian ritual to try to revive Chiara, then hid it in a Quay shrine.
Inscriptions suggest the Ankh was a gift from the Vaal, likely via a survivor of the Fall.
Veruso outlawed thaumaturgy and burned those who practised it.
Veruso had the virtue gems collected and buried beneath Highgate, sealed and forgotten.
Gems were buried in sealed caverns under Highgate; later mined by Chitus' slaves.
Veruso was tested by a Lord's Trial to become leader of the Azmeri.
Caspiro was the only survivor of a labyrinth trial that killed Veruso's only son.
Caspiro was chosen by Lord's Trial as successor.
Without a clear heir, Alano Phrecia was crowned after avenging Caspiro.
A 'dark being' (identified by the GGG Lore Q&A with the darkness housed in the Vaal Oversoul) dismembered Caspiro.
Alano's legions drove the dark being into its lair and sealed it away in 35 IC.
Alano led the victory over the dark being.
Alano's victory led to the unbroken Phrecian imperial line.
Alano began the unbroken line of Phrecian emperors ending with Izaro.
Romira Phrecian was an emperor of the Phrecian line.
Tyndarus reigned in the Phrecian line.
Romira was deposed by the burning of Sarn.
Sarn was burned to the ground and rebuilt.
Sarn's later festivals commemorating the Night of a Thousand Ribbons hosted Chitus' assassination in 1334 IC (the date of Romira's reign is not given in the corpus).
Chitus was killed during the festival celebration.
Trarthus was an imperial exile colony.
The war was fought in Trarthus.
Izaro built the Lord's Labyrinth to let the Goddess of Justice choose his successor.
